---
title: "Beta and Dirichlet: random probability vectors"
subtitle: "Catalog P-01, P-02 · rungs 1–2 · after Broderick (MLSS 2016, part I)"
description: "Draw random weight vectors again and again, and watch the parameter a decide between all-or-nothing and nearly even."
toc: false
---

A mixture needs weights: nonnegative numbers that add up to one. The Dirichlet distribution
is a distribution over such vectors. With K = 2 it is the Beta distribution: rho_1 ~
Beta(a_1, a_2) and rho_2 = 1 − rho_1. Its parameters work like pseudo-counts: E(rho_k) =
a_k / (a_1 + … + a_K), and the larger they are, the closer each draw stays to that mean.


## What to try

- **K = 2 (Beta).** Press **Draw again** (or Enter) a few times, or switch on auto-draw.
  At a = 1 every value of rho_1 is equally likely. At a = 0.01 almost every draw puts
  nearly all weight on one of the two components. At a = 1000 both stay near one half.
  The right panel shows the Beta density with the current rho_1 in red.
- **K = 5 to 12 (Dirichlet).** The same rule with more components: small a concentrates
  each draw on one or two components, large a flattens it towards 1/K (dashed line).
- **K = 3 and the ternary view.** Every draw is a point in a triangle whose corners are
  (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0) and (0, 0, 1). The presets show the three shapes: a = 0.5 pushes
  the points into the corners, a = 5 gathers them in the centre, and a = (40, 10, 10) pulls
  them towards rho_1 = 40/60 = 2/3.
- **set each a_k** gives every component its own parameter.

As K grows and a shrinks with K·a held fixed, the Dirichlet draw starts to look like the
stick-breaking weights of the Dirichlet process ([paintbox](paintbox.qmd),
[stick-breaking](stick-breaking.qmd)).

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
After Broderick (MLSS 2016, part I, demos 1 and 2); the mathematics is re-implemented and
no code is copied.
